highlights.title: Another lab's review, finding by finding
highlights.text: When your other provider reviews a thread's change, each thing it finds gets a number, and the thread has to answer every one: fixed, disputed with why, or left for you. The done card lists them with what was done, and the phone and website show them too.

media.alt: A done card with "Reviewed by Codex (codex-main), 2 rounds: passed" and three findings: two with green ticks marked Fixed with what changed, and one with an orange mark marked Disputed with the thread's reason.

highlights.title: Parts of a project
highlights.text: A project can be a part of another: Make a Part of in the project's menu. A part folds under its parent in the sidebar and is listed on the parent's page, and its threads are told the parent's goals as well as its own.

media.alt: The Threadbear project's page. Photo sync is made a part of Threadbear: it leaves the sidebar's list, a Parts section with Photo sync appears at the top of the page, and opening Threadbear's row in the sidebar shows its threads with Photo sync folded under them.

highlights.title: Projects: a row each, and tabs on the page
highlights.text: With the Decisions experiment on, the sidebar's Projects list is one row a project, with its decisions or thread count, and its arrow shows the threads. A project's page has Decisions and Project tabs; ⇧⌘[ and ⇧⌘] step between them.

media.alt: The Projects sidebar with a row for each of Photo sync, Threadbear, Walkies and Not in a project. Threadbear's and Photo sync's arrows open and fold their threads, then clicking Threadbear opens its page on the Decisions tab with its questions; the Project tab shows its goals, state and notes, then it goes back to Decisions.

highlights.title: Usage's weekly charts show the whole week
highlights.text: Each login's weekly chart in the Usage panel shows the last seven days with their names along the bottom, and breaks the line where the week reset. A switch in the panel's Settings card hides Weekly Fable.

media.alt: A login in the Usage panel at its 5-hour limit, with a weekly chart from Friday to Saturday whose line jumps up at Sunday's reset and runs on dotted to when it would run out, and under it a Settings card with a Show Weekly Fable switch.

added: Search finds a thread by what it's about, not just its title: the librarian gives each thread a few search words, so "dentist" finds "Wisdom tooth meeting location". On the phone, search also looks through every message

added.text: The phone app shows a plan in full: a plan card that opens it in a sheet, with Copy and Share, and Go ahead on Claude's plan card

added: Click a picture's chip or thumbnail in the message box to look at it in Quick Look
Schedule… in the message box's + menu opens a new schedule with what you've typed
A link to another site in a patch's panel opens in your browser (or over the panel, as your web links setting says), and the panel's bar gets a Back button
A quiet inbox: threads another thread started archive themselves once they're finished, and a thread waiting only on its helpers hibernates until they're done (an experiment)
changed: Move to another machine is on for everyone, no longer an experiment
Reply buttons, schedule checks and standing instructions are on for everyone, no longer experiments
The recap box on threads quiet for 12 hours is gone, after a day of trying it
A pool thread that ran out of room carries on as soon as any login in its pool has room again, and a login is used down to 1% left rather than 10%
The agent hears which of its reply buttons you pressed, so it doesn't do the same job again
Pasting several lines into the Terminal asks first, when the shell would run each line as it arrived

changed.text: Builds and tests Threadbear starts run at low priority rather than in the background, which was far too slow on some Macs; jobPriority in runner.json picks

changed: The runner starts a couple of seconds faster
Messages from Android say they came from the phone app, not the iPhone app
The done card counts work pushed to a branch but not merged as still open (with the loose ends experiment on)

The new app for Mac, Windows and Linux (an experiment) caught up on most of this one: the Terminal, Settings, Scheduled, Usage, the options review window, the limit box, videos and PDFs in the side pane, panels that glide, and sends that wait out a runner restart. It also shows the model a sub-agent runs on, keeps your last 24 threads ready so switching back is instant, and installs its updates by itself
fixed: Closing the Terminal could leave the thread blank until you switched threads
An archived thread could leave a gap in the inbox for a few seconds on a busy Mac
The context ring's popover could run down past the bottom of the window

fixed.text: The slash command list stays on the screen the message box is on, and goes under the box when there's more room there

fixed: A long wait line between turns stays on one line
A long project name in the sidebar no longer runs under a row's hover buttons

fixed.text: A home patch could make an Auto thread ask before every file edit; now only the commands it really runs count, and the card says which patch
Two logins on the same email in a shared pool are no longer merged into one
Joining a second Mac: tb is on the PATH, the host name it prints works, and ssh failures say what went wrong

fixed: Picking another login or folder between turns no longer stops the agent's sub-agents

fixed.text: On Windows, the new app names files by their normal drive path, so links to files open there
Threadbear's guard on its own secrets folder caught fewer spellings than it should: other capital letters, and the runner's home variable

fixed: Closed several security holes, including a schedule edit that could approve a changed check, a repository's own git settings running from the done card's check, and a web panel's page opening browser tabs by itself
